solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The wrong character, perhaps, to race on motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the race follows the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written MI in crosswords
to race is to sprint

explanation.surface: A driver racing on a motorway is the wrong sort of character to have on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a printed letter, not a person; M1 is London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo puts a wrong letter on the page, and 'perhaps' flags that this is one kind of error.

clue.text: Smooth youth leader's gentle mockery

parts.note: to smooth clothes is to iron them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of youth is used

explanation.surface: A slick young leader is teased with mild sarcasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what you mean is a mild, wry form of ridicule.

clue.text: Emergency device working in cap, though not when raised

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of in cap are being worked into a new order

parts.note: though means but

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards, so the letters of not run backwards

explanation.surface: An alarm switch fitted in a cap works, except when the cap is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges IN CAP into PANIC; 'when raised' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the switch pressed in a crisis to summon help or stop a machine.

clue.text: Brood at home, worried about youngster

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the youngster

parts.note: being in means being at home
worried, as in 'what's eating you?', gives ate
a cub is a young animal or a junior scout

explanation.surface: A parent stays home, fretting over a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' as ate is the sense in 'what's eating you?'; 'Brood' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood eggs is to sit on them keeping them warm until they hatch.

clue.text: Cashiers least disposed to swallow most of party's tall stories

indicators.note: the cashiers swallow, taking the shortened party inside them

parts.note: bank cashiers are tellers

indicators.note: most of a word drops its final letter

parts.note: a rave is a party; the 's just links it

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of least are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bank clerks, not keen on believing a partygoer's exaggerated stories.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a rave is a large all-night dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts brought back by voyagers have long been proverbial for being exaggerated or invented.

clue.text: Fruit headmaster initially introduced into French school

indicators.note: introduced into means the letter is placed inside the school

parts.note: a lycée is a French secondary school

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of headmaster

explanation.surface: A head teacher brings a fruit into a French school.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small Chinese fruit with a rough red skin and white flesh.

clue.text: Stripper has old Charlie gripped by lecherous desire!

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the desire

parts.note: lust is lecherous desire
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A striptease artist and an old man called Charlie, caught up in lust.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is not a dancer: swarms of these insects strip crops bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming grasshoppers devour every leaf in a field, stripping vegetation.

clue.text: Vehicle taking armoured troops to north

indicators.note: in a down clue going to the north reads the letters upwards

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Armoured Corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying tank troops northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor vehicle for carrying passengers on roads, the commonest sort.

clue.text: Oddball caught with little money in Morecambe

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, of Morecambe and Wise
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A weirdo is arrested with a bit of cash in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort, but it stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person whose behaviour is odd or unconventional.

clue.text: Scam involving grandad's first bill for drink

indicators.note: involving means the scam wraps around that letter

parts.note: a con is a scam

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of grandad's

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A con trick in which grandad is landed with the bar bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy from the Cognac region of France, sipped after dinner.

clue.text: Precision recognised in a key church office

parts.note: C is a musical key
a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: Exactness is valued in a key church post.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean exactness or correctness in measuring or aiming.

clue.text: Decline verbally, showing brief togetherness

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: to decline is to sink

explanation.surface: Refusing out loud shows only a brief unity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refusing but means going down.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a shortening of synchronisation, things moving in step together.

clue.text: Part of skeleton of second animal maybe one found across river?

indicators.note: the pieces are found across, spanning the river letter

parts.note: a beast is an animal, the maybe because it is a loose term
B denotes second class or second grade
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bone from a second beast, discovered on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum, the flat bone in the chest where the ribs meet, is one of the skeleton's bones.

clue.text: In spring she sat rocking family pet, perhaps

indicators.note: In puts the rearranged letters inside the spring

parts.note: to spring is to bound

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters of she sat into a new order

explanation.surface: In spring she sat in a rocking chair with the family dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-eared, short-legged dog breed is often kept as a household pet; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Disproof concerning what Jeeves would do, we hear

parts.note: re means concerning

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said aloud

parts.note: Jeeves, P G Wodehouse's famous manservant, would butle, act as a butler

explanation.surface: A refutation about how Jeeves behaves, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: To butle is a jokey verb for working as a butler.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is an argument that counters or disproves a claim.

clue.text: Leader's time going over report of Oxford college

indicators.note: in a down clue going over turns the word upwards

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

indicators.note: report of means the college name is spoken

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: The head of an Oxford college runs over time on a report.
explanation.walkthrough: In British papers a 'leader' is the leading article, giving the paper's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article states the paper's own opinion on a topic.

clue.text: Reportedly one who was bound to explore the internet

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a serf was a medieval labourer bound to the land

explanation.surface: A captive, it is said, set off exploring the web.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse from site to site online is called surfing the web.

clue.text: Practical joke involving a nurse once upset certain Asians

indicators.note: involving means the joke wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a jape is a practical joke

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a British nursing grade now abolished

explanation.surface: A prank involving a former nurse upset some Asian visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' is there because the State Enrolled Nurse grade no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people from Japan, one particular Asian nation.

clue.text: Suggestion made by husband in jest, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of jest

explanation.surface: A husband drops a suggestion while joking, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a slight indication or a piece of advice.

clue.text: Condition recognised by chemists first of all in 1811-20?

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the period

parts.note: the Regency was the period when the future George IV ruled as Prince Regent

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of all

explanation.surface: A state of affairs first noticed by pharmacists in the Regency era.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists speak of the quality of acting as a reagent, a substance that takes part in a reaction.

clue.text: One's left, for example, in flimsy clothing

definitions.note: read as one is left: something left behind

indicators.note: clothing means the flimsy word dresses round the other letters

parts.note: lacy fabric is delicate and flimsy

explanation.surface: A person goes out wearing very little, flimsy clothing for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' is the containment signal, not clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is what a person leaves to heirs in a will.

clue.text: Small picture in vessel, one next to a shrub

indicators.note: in places the small picture inside the vessel

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
an inset is a small picture set within a larger one
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A little painting in a pot, placed beside a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant with red leaf-like bracts is a Christmas favourite and a shrub in the wild.

clue.text: In Idaho, a rare type of frost

indicators.note: In shows the letters sit inside the words Idaho, a rare

explanation.surface: Idaho gets an unusual frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarfrost is the white feathery coating of ice that forms on cold nights.

clue.text: Greek screen with ends cut off

indicators.note: with ends cut off removes the first and last letters of the screen word

parts.note: a lattice is a screen of crossed strips

explanation.surface: A Greek screen trimmed at both edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means of Attica or Athens, so Greek in the classical sense.

clue.text: Bonanza wife and daughter dipped into in autumn

indicators.note: the pair is dipped into, so the next word goes between them

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A windfall that a wife and daughter spent from in the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is an unexpected piece of good fortune or money.

clue.text: Study conclusion of Iliad in French

indicators.note: conclusion of takes the last letter of Iliad

parts.note: en is French for in

explanation.surface: A study of how Homer's Iliad ends, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A study is a private room for working, also called a den.

clue.text: Legal right — what a woman may fight for, not a man

indicators.note: not means the man is left out

parts.words: what a woman may fight for
parts.note: women campaign for equal rights with men
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A legal claim that women campaign for and men do not.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, equity is the body of fairness principles that supplements common law, giving a right.

clue.text: Boy catching large fish

indicators.note: catching means the boy's name holds the letter

parts.note: Benny is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy hooks a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small, spiny-finned fish of rock pools and shallows.

clue.text: Female by chance catching tail of crested duck

parts.note: she is a female pronoun

indicators.note: catching means luck holds that letter

parts.note: luck is chance

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here of crested

explanation.surface: A female, by chance, catches the tail of a crested duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crested' looks like part of the definition, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large black, white and chestnut duck of coasts and estuaries.
